=== FINDING 3 (NEW, BLOCKING in my view): 03821d7 makes every ordinary "merge main" commit subject to the lane-ownership check, which will make claude-lane branches unmergeable the first time main carries a codex-lane file. ===
commit_files() is not used only by _is_record_only_commit. check_lanes() calls it for LANE DISCIPLINE: for every file, `cls = classify_path(f); if cls == "shared": ... elif cls != agent: errors.append("touches '<f>', outside the <agent> lane")`. Before 03821d7 a merge commit returned ZERO files (that is the very blindness this commit fixes), so merges were silently exempt from lane ownership. After it, a merge returns its entire first-parent diff -- I measured 30 files for PR #51's merge 7d6836af -- and every one of them is now attributed to the merging agent.
Today that is harmless only by luck: I checked those 30 files and none classify as `codex` (plugins/*/lwb/vendor/** classifies as `shared`, which absorbs most of it). It is one codex-lane commit on main away from biting. Demonstrated rather than asserted: with commit_files stubbed to return ['adapters/codex/hook_io.py', 'HANDOFF.md'] for that same merge, check_lanes emits
  FAIL: 7d6836afe842 (LWB-Agent: claude): touches 'adapters/codex/hook_io.py', outside the claude lane and not a shared path
(I stubbed the FILE LIST, not the logic -- the real merge carried no codex-lane file. What is not stubbed is that commit_files now really does return the full first-parent diff for a merge, which is what puts such a file in that list the moment main has one.)
Merging main is not optional here -- it is the prescribed way to clear a merge conflict, and force-push is denied -- so this failure mode has no escape hatch: the branch could not be fixed, only abandoned and re-cut. That is the same "unsatisfiable gate" failure reviews/README.md already says is worse than a strict one.
NARROW FIX: skip the lane-ownership loop for a commit with 2+ parents (a merge introduces no authorship of its own; the commits it brings were each checked on their own branch), while still using the first-parent diff for _is_record_only_commit. That keeps 03821d7's real fix and drops its side effect.

=== 03821d7's OWN FIX IS CORRECT, and I checked the thing that would make it dangerous ===
The reasoning is sound and I verified the part that matters: a merge's first-parent diff is the total change to the resulting tree, so a merge whose first-parent diff is empty cannot be hiding content brought in via a second parent -- there is nothing to smuggle, because the result tree equals the first parent's. Using `-m` instead would have been wrong for exactly the reason the docstring gives. The "merge carrying real content alongside a review record is NOT skipped" case is tested, which is the regression that would have mattered most. 601 tests pass at this head (595 + 6), and FINDING 1 is unchanged: lwb_check_state_claims.py still exits 1 on HANDOFF.md's 22/22 against 23 proof records, and CI still reports exactly lwb-check-state-claims and lwb-lanes as the failing steps. === FINDING 2 (BLOCKING in my view, and NOT mentioned anywhere in the PR): a DISAGREE from an independent reviewer stops being able to block the merge. ===
The PR body says "Nothing about the freshness check, the AGREE-verdict check, the reviewer_id != commit_author_id check, the segment-collision check, or the dispatched-boolean requirement was weakened." That is true per-record and false at the gate. Every rejection reason _review_ok produces -- not just STALE -- is routed into the local list and downgraded to a NOTICE once enough valid records exist. Measured directly against this branch's own code, REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS=1, one valid AGREE plus one other record in the same directory:
    valid AGREE + DISAGREE record      -> ok=True, errors=0, 1 notice
    valid AGREE + SELF-REVIEW record   -> ok=True, errors=0, 1 notice   (reviewer_id == commit_author_id)
    valid AGREE + MALFORMED JSON       -> ok=True, errors=0, 1 notice
Before this change all three failed the build. The first line is the one that matters: TODAY, a DISAGREE record fails lwb-lanes, which is why #44 and #40 are red and why my own DISAGREE on #52 is load-bearing. AFTER this change, any single AGREE at the same head silently outvotes any number of DISAGREEs, with a NOTICE in a log that nothing fails on -- and this repository has already written down, in reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md, what it thinks of "a NOTICE in a log that nothing fails on" as a safeguard.
I am NOT claiming the old behaviour was the designed one; reviews/README.md says only "only AGREE satisfies the gate", never that a DISAGREE vetoes, so the veto may well have been an accident of the same conflation this PR fixes. That is exactly why it needs to be an explicit decision by the owner and written into reviews/README.md, not an unremarked side effect of a bug fix whose text says nothing was weakened. Two reviewers disagreeing about the same head is a state D27 exists to produce; what the gate should do with it is a policy question.
NARROWER ALTERNATIVE, if the owner wants dissent to keep blocking: escalate to `errors` only the reasons that are not "this record is superseded" -- i.e. keep STALE (and perhaps only STALE) as a notice, leave DISAGREE, identity collision and malformed JSON fatal. That is a one-line predicate on the local list and it fixes the deadlock without changing what a DISAGREE means.
